input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: All calls to the same decorated function now share one statistics dict, and each call clears it at entry. Overlapping calls from different threads corrupt each other's counters, and the earlier call's statistics are wiped mid-run.
- rationale: Trigger: two threads (or overlapping invocations) call the same @retry-decorated function at once. Mechanism: the second call runs stats.clear() and then both copies write into the same dict, where previously each call got its own dict via copy.statistics. Impact: statistics read from wrapped_f.statistics or the first call's retry state show mixed or reset attempt counts, a silent wrong result. Retry decisions use per-call retry state, so the damage is limited to reported statistics.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label: one statistics dict is shared and cleared on every call instead of being created per call. When calls overlap, the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's data, and both calls end up writing into the same dict. The trigger and the impact (corrupted or merged statistics) also match.
